html:
Gandhara Buddhist art is the stone and stucco sculpture made in Gandhara, around Peshawar and Taxila, from about the 1st to the 5th century CE. It gave the world some of the first images of the Buddha in human form.

For centuries Buddhists had shown the Buddha only by signs: a footprint, an empty seat, a wheel. Under the Kushan Empire, and above all under King Kanishka in the 2nd century, sculptors in Gandhara and in Mathura began to carve him as a man.

The Gandhara style mixes two worlds. The Buddha has wavy hair, a straight nose and a robe with heavy folds like a Roman toga. The sculptors drew on the Greek tradition left by the Indo-Greek kingdoms and on trade with the Roman world. The subject and the meaning are Indian.

Monks and merchants carried the image along the Silk Road. The Buddhas of Bamiyan and the cave shrines of China grew from it. The art faded after the Huna invasions wrecked the monasteries of Gandhara around 500.
sum: Gandhara Buddhist art is the stone and stucco sculpture made in Gandhara, around Peshawar and Taxila, from about the 1st to the 5th century CE. It gave the world some of the first images of the Buddha in human form.
